Ashwin Rao: quick q — after PTQ to INT8 on rerank-v2 I'm seeing ndcg@10 drop ~1.7% vs fp16 on ms-marco dev. MRR almost unchanged. anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
Maria Chen: did you run the exact same eval harness + tokenization? small tokenization differences can shift ndcg a lot even if mrr stays similar.
Ashwin Rao: yep same harness binary. command i ran:
```
./eval_rerank --model rerank-v2-int8 --data ms-marco-dev --metric ndcg@10,mrr@10 --topk 10 --seed 42 --tokenizer redwood-v2
```
Maria Chen: can you paste the eval-bot job id? did the job use the cached embeddings or reran from scratch?
eval-bot: Completed job 304: ndcg@10=0.812 (-0.017), mrr@10=0.621 (-0.002). runtime 12m.
Leila Duarte: two quick suspects: 1) quantization-induced calibration changes in logits (softmax scale), 2) truncation differences at doc boundaries changing input lengths.
Omar Khan: also check whether the candidate generation step changed (e.g., topk for the generator). If the candidate set quality changed, reranker ndcg will move even without model changes.
Ashwin Rao: generator is same. candidates unchanged. i dumped a few failure cases — seems to be higher weight on long docs getting ranked slightly lower.
Kevin Patel: interesting. could be KV-cache/attn precision mismatch for long sequences with INT8. Try: 1) run per-length slices, 2) eval ndcg@5 and ndcg@100 to see where it moves.
Maria Chen: recommended quick triage:
- run bootstrap significance test (n=1000) on ndcg deltas
- split queries by token-length quartiles
- run a pure-scoring test (no softmax) to compare relative logits ordering
Leila Duarte: for the scoring test you can do a pairwise Kendall tau between fp16 logits and int8 logits on the same candidate list. if tau drops -> ordering issue.
Ashwin Rao: running bootstrap now (background). also running an fp16->int8 cross-score: just comparing logits.
Leila Duarte: watch out for normalization layers — we saw similar with a reranker before where LayerNorm scale got folded differently during PTQ and ranking shifted.
Omar Khan: can you repro with a small synthetic subset: 1k queries, deterministic seeds, dump logits for each candidate. that makes statistical tests easier.
Ashwin Rao: good call. i'll run 1k deterministic, dump logits + lengths.
Kevin Patel: another quick probe: eval with quantized softmax temperature sweep. sometimes a uniform temperature correction recovers ndcg without changing MRR.
Maria Chen: +1. also try per-head sensitivity: quantize only weights but keep activations fp16 for a run. helps isolate activation quantization impact.
Ashwin Rao: noted. plan: (1) 1k-deterministic dump, (2) tau + bootstrap, (3) length-sliced ndcg, (4) int4 sanity check. anyone want to own the bootstrap code?
Leila Duarte: i'll drop a small python snippet you can reuse:
```python
# bootstrap ndcg delta
import random, numpy as np
def bootstrap_delta(metric_vals_fp, metric_vals_q, n=1000):
    deltas=[]
    N=len(metric_vals_fp)
    for _ in range(n):
        idx = np.random.randint(0, N, N)
        deltas.append(np.mean(metric_vals_q[idx]) - np.mean(metric_vals_fp[idx]))
    return np.percentile(deltas, [2.5, 97.5]), np.mean(deltas)
```
Ashwin Rao: perfect, thanks.
eval-bot: Started job 305 (1k-dump, deterministic). ETA ~8m.
Omar Khan: after you have dumps, run Kendall tau and also compute per-query delta then histogram it. if a few queries dominate, that points to dataset slice issues.
Kevin Patel: for dataset slices, check head vs tail, and also queries with many relevant docs vs single-relevance. ndcg is sensitive to multiple relevant docs being shuffled.
Maria Chen: last thing — double-check the tokenization output for the same doc between fp16 and int8 runs. tokenizers can be nondet if using different versions. a 1-token shift at query boundary can change scores for short docs.
Ashwin Rao: all good points. i'll post dumps + quick stats here when done. thanks everyone. :rocket:
Leila Duarte: if we can't find a quantization bug, we can try an affine output scale correction trained on a small calibration set — that fixed a 0.8% ndcg regression for a previous model.
Ashwin Rao: noted, will try calibration if diagnostic suggests a scale shift.
Maria Chen: also add an eval to compute normalized discounted cumulative error (relative to fp16) per query — helps visualize magnitude.
